themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK vs. a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% surge (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a potential contamination event or system failure affecting Far Rockaway residents' drinking water.
evidence: 4 water quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% spike)
Z-score of 11.72 indicates statistically extreme deviation—highest severity classification
Aligns with historical CB budget requests for DEP capital projects addressing water infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Interview NYC DEP about what triggered the spike and whether residents need to boil water or seek alternative sources
Investigate whether aging water mains or recent construction (422 DOB permits filed) may have caused contamination
Cross-check with health department to determine if poison control or hospital admissions for water-borne illness have spiked in parallel

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs jumped to 20 complaints THIS WEEK vs. a 3.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (540% spike, z-score: 8.08), and dangling signs hit 13 THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 average (197% spike)—indicating systemic infrastructure deterioration in the district.
evidence: 20 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score: 8.08)
13 dangling street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly baseline (197% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Combined signal suggests weather event or deferred maintenance affecting multiple infrastructure assets
reporting_angles: Examine whether recent storms or ocean spray (Rockaways peninsula exposure) accelerated corrosion of signage
Interview DOT about maintenance schedules and budget constraints for Far Rockaway's aging street infrastructure
Assess safety risks: are missing or dangling signs creating navigation hazards or liability for the city?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints doubled to 20 LAST WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly average (105% spike, z-score: 2.97), and abandoned vehicle complaints hit 42 two weeks ago vs. 20.9 average (101% spike)—signaling emerging public nuisance and blight concentrated over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 20 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly baseline (105% spike, z-score: 2.97)
42 abandoned vehicle complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 20.9 weekly baseline (101% spike, z-score: 2.71)
Abandoned vehicles rank 9th in 90-day complaint volume (289 total), indicating chronic issue now accelerating
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD/DOT Tow on whether they're understaffed or facing towing infrastructure bottlenecks in the Rockaways
Investigate whether economic downturn or post-holiday season is driving abandonment of vehicles in this lower-income district
Document the blight impact: are residents reporting these vehicles as squatting sites, chop shops, or public safety hazards?

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 4 LAST WEEK vs. a 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 7.0), suggesting either disease spread, storm damage, or inadequate maintenance of the district's urban forest.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 7.0)
Parks capital budget requests appear repeatedly in CB agenda, suggesting chronic underinvestment in tree maintenance
Rockaways' coastal location exposes trees to salt spray and storm damage—vulnerability may be accelerating
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks on recent tree diseases or pest infestations detected in Far Rockaway
Investigate whether recent storms or seasonal salt damage caused the spike
Report on equitable tree canopy coverage: does Far Rockaway have fewer trees per capita than other NYC districts?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints increased to 21 LAST WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly average (66% spike, z-score: 2.68), adding to the already high baseline of 1,167 residential noise complaints over 90 days and suggesting construction or nightlife disruption.
evidence: 21 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly baseline (66% spike, z-score: 2.68)
Residential noise is the 2nd largest complaint category (1,167 total over 90 days), suggesting chronic quality-of-life issue
422 DOB permits filed in 90 days—construction activity may be driving spike in outdoor noise
reporting_angles: Examine whether active construction sites (154 new buildings, 235 alterations filed) are operating outside permitted hours
Interview residents about whether recent development (Edgemere Commons, Arverne East projects) has disrupted nighttime peace
Check if local bars or venues have expanded outdoor service, driving late-night noise complaints
